message.content:
Since \(\mathbf{b}\) bisects the angle between \(\mathbf{a}\) and \(\mathbf{c}\), the direction of \(\mathbf{c}\) is the reflection of \(\mathbf{a}\) across the line spanned by \(\mathbf{b}\).

The reflection of \(\mathbf{a}\) across the line through \(\mathbf{b}\) is
\[
\mathbf{a}' = 2\frac{\mathbf{a}\cdot \mathbf{b}}{\mathbf{b}\cdot \mathbf{b}}\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a}.
\]
Now
\[
\mathbf{a}\cdot \mathbf{b}=7(3)+(-1)(1)+4(2)=28,
\]
and
\[
\mathbf{b}\cdot \mathbf{b}=3^2+1^2+2^2=14.
\]
So
\[
\mathbf{a}'=2\cdot \frac{28}{14}\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a}
=4\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a}.
\]
Thus
\[
\mathbf{a}'=4\begin{pmatrix}3\\1\\2\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}7\\-1\\4\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}12-7\\4+1\\8-4\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}5\\5\\4\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Therefore \(\mathbf{c}\) is a scalar multiple of \(\begin{pmatrix}5\\5\\4\end{pmatrix}\).

Also \(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathbf{c}\) are collinear, so
\[
\mathbf{c}=\mathbf{a}+t(\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a})
=\begin{pmatrix}7\\-1\\4\end{pmatrix}
+t\begin{pmatrix}-4\\2\\-2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Set
\[
\begin{pmatrix}7-4t\\-1+2t\\4-2t\end{pmatrix}
=
k\begin{pmatrix}5\\5\\4\end{pmatrix}.
\]
From the first two coordinates,
\[
7-4t=5k,\qquad -1+2t=5k.
\]
Subtracting gives
\[
8-6t=0 \implies t=\frac43.
\]
Then
\[
5k=-1+2\cdot \frac43=\frac53,
\]
so
\[
k=\frac13.
\]
Hence
\[
\mathbf{c}=\frac13\begin{pmatrix}5\\5\\4\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}\frac53\\[2pt]\frac53\\[2pt]\frac43\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}\frac53\\[2pt]\frac53\\[2pt]\frac43\end{pmatrix}}\).
